transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Anna Lee (Redwood AE), Mike Chan (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (CTO, Acme), Tom Alvarez (Eng Mgr, Acme), Jorge Morales (Procurement, Acme)

Summary: quick signoff on success criteria, clarified workload sizing and benchmarking plan, acceptance test thresholds and reporting format, next steps on data access and procurement.

00:00 Anna: okay everyone thanks for hopping on, uh this is Anna from Redwood. Mike from the SE team is here too. we wanted to run through the POC success criteria and make sure we have the go/no-go thresholds nailed down.
00:12 Priya: yep, thanks Anna. we've got Tom and Jorge from our side. main goals: accurate clinical note summarization, sub-200ms median latency at p95-ish for our interactive UI, and predictable cost per 1k tokens — those are the top metrics for execs.
00:28 Mike: great. just to set expectations, our POC will include three workloads: interactive summarization (low latency), nightly batch embedding for search (throughput), and reranking for clinical alerts (accuracy-focused). we'll size based on the QPS profile you sent previously but need the sample slices.
00:47 Tom: i uploaded a sample in the slack thread yesterday, but it's redacted. is that enough for you to run a baseline?
00:55 Mike: should be enough if the stats align. we'll ask for 10 representative samples across lengths: short (<=200 tokens), medium (200-1200), long (>1200) — helps with KV cache effects and sequence-length tail.
01:10 Priya: got it. quick question on the latency threshold: you said p95 200ms, is that realistic on hosted vs dedicated?
01:20 Anna: yes that's one of the tradeoffs we want to capture in the success criteria. hosted can hit lower time-to-value but dedicated or private deployment gives more consistent p95 under load. for the POC we can benchmark on both modes — we'll propose a hosted run first and if you want we can reserve a small dedicated pool for a head-to-head.
01:38 Jorge: procurement question — will sending sample data to hosted service cause compliance issues? we have patient-adjacent data, need SOC2 + HIPAA considerations.
01:47 Anna: understood. we'll use encrypted channels and we can sign the DPA/NDA. Redwood Private option (VPC) is available if you need customer-managed keys and no data egress. we will also provide our SOC 2 report and KMS integration doc.
02:05 Priya: great, please share those docs. also we need to define acceptance tests for quality: what's the go/no-go on summarization accuracy?
02:15 Mike: recommended approach — we'll run evals using your gold set (n=200 ideally) and calculate ROUGE/L- or prefer EM/precision/recall depending on task. for clinical summarization we'll propose a combined threshold: F1 >= 0.82 and human review pass-rate >= 90% on a stratified sample. if either metric fails, we flag for quality regression.
02:36 Tom: 0.82 seems ok but can we add a manual review requirement for high-risk notes? like if the model flags uncertainty.
02:44 Mike: yes, we'll include an uncertainty threshold and show a sample of failure cases in the report.
03:00 Anna: on reporting format — we will deliver a single POC report with: executive summary, benchmark tables (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput QPS, cost per 1k tokens), quality evals (metrics + sample failures), and a pass/fail verdict per success criteria with notes. we'll share the report as a PDF and a CSV of raw runs.
03:22 Priya: that sounds good. can you show an example of the pass/fail table?
03:28 Mike: sure — for this POC we'll have rows for each criterion: latency, quality, throughput, cost. each row has target, observed, and verdict. e.g. latency target p95 <= 200ms (hosted) ; observed p95 180ms ; verdict PASS. if observed p95 is > 250ms we'd mark FAIL and recommend next steps.
03:49 Jorge: vendor comparison — are you going to compare against Anthropic or OpenAI in the report?
03:55 Anna: we can run a competitive baseline if you want. note that it adds runs and costs; but useful for procurement. we'll include competitor tests as a separate appendix if you sign off.
04:10 Tom: workload sizing — we need to confirm the QPS shape. Priya, our expected peak is 150 qps for the UI, sustained 30 qps, with nightly batch of 2M tokens. does that sound right?
04:23 Priya: yes that's the ballpark. for POC we want scaled-down runs: 10 qps sustained + 100 qps short bursts to simulate spikes.
04:33 Mike: perfect. for benchmarking we'll run short stress tests (5-10 minutes) at burst rates and longer 1-hour sustained runs at target sustained rate to capture autoscaling behavior. also will capture KV cache hit rates — sometimes transcriber reads K-V as K-V cash in notes — but it's kv-cache.
04:55 Priya: ha, yes. any known outliers we should watch for?
05:00 Mike: long sequence tails: >1k tokens increase compute; quantized models reduce cost but may impact quality — we'll include model variants in the runs: baseline open model, quantized variant, and any Redwood-verified optimized variant.
05:18 Anna: timeline: we agreed POC kickoff once data and SSO/DPA are in place. proposed timeline: share data by 2025-11-10, Redwood runs benchmarks and shares preliminary report by 2025-11-12 to 11-14, final report and exec review by 2025-11-18. does that work?
05:36 Priya: yes that fits our internal timelines. Procurement to align NDA/contract by 2025-11-14.
05:44 Jorge: noted.
05:48 Tom: acceptance criteria recap — can we state them now so we have signoff?
05:54 Anna: sure. i will read them; please say yes/no. 1) Latency: p95 for interactive summarization <= 200ms on hosted baseline or <= 180ms on dedicated; 2) Quality: summarization F1 >= 0.82 and human pass-rate >= 90% on sampled notes; 3) Throughput: batch job completes within nightly window (<= 2 hours for 2M tokens scaled down for test); 4) Cost: projected token cost <= $X per 1k tokens (we'll fill real number in doc) or lower than current baseline by 20%; 5) Security: data handling meets SOC2/HIPAA as evidenced by provided docs and DPA signed.
06:34 Priya: yes to 1,2,3 and 5. on cost we need to see the numbers — so conditional yes.
06:42 Tom: same, conditional on concrete numbers.
06:45 Anna: understood — we'll put an explicit cost projection and sensitivity analysis in the report.
06:52 Mike: acceptance test mechanics: we'll run N runs per model variant, collect metrics, produce CSV of raw latencies, and a human-audited sample of 50 notes for the quality pass-rate. pass if all criteria meet targets, else fail and we list mitigation options.
07:12 Priya: for reporting frequency during the POC can you provide a mid-run status update?
07:18 Anna: yes — mid-run status after first benchmark day (expected 2025-11-12) and final report by 2025-11-18.
07:27 Jorge: procurement question — please send your standard SOW template and pricing sheet.
07:31 Anna: will do.
07:34 Tom: any open technical blockers?
07:36 Mike: only access to the sanitized datasets and a VPN credential if we need VPC testing. if you prefer hosted we can do that first, then VPC. also will need sample app traffic profile (headers, tokens per request).
07:51 Priya: we'll share traffic profile and dataset slices by 2025-11-10.
07:55 Mike: perfect. last item — monitoring and observability in the report: we'll include per-route token breakdown, p50/p95/p99, KV cache stats, batching efficiency, and cost per token breakdown.
08:12 Anna: ok to recap next steps: Anna send updated success criteria doc and pass/fail table; Mike run baseline benchmarks once data received; Priya share datasets and traffic profile; Jorge handle NDA/contract timeline.
08:28 Priya: fine.
08:30 Anna: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the doc and links to security artifacts.
08:36 Tom: thanks all.

End of call.
